s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive heart failure with exertional dyspnea and signs of fluid overload
key_facts: Baseline functional status until 2 months ago
P wave preceding every QRS with 1:1 relationship
Elevated brain-type natriuretic peptide at 1700 pg/mL
Severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction on echocardiogram

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive heart failure with exertional dyspnea and signs of fluid overload
key_facts: Baseline functional status until 2 months ago
P wave preceding every QRS with 1:1 relationship
Elevated brain-type natriuretic peptide at 1700 pg/mL

differentials: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
per_call: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response

shortlist.label: Tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Narrow complex tachycardia and severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction

shortlist.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction and signs of fluid overload

shortlist.label: Restrictive cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Grade 2 diastolic dysfunction and severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction

shortlist.label: Cardiac amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated brain-type natriuretic peptide and severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction

shortlist.label: Atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Narrow complex tachycardia with P wave preceding every QRS

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and echocardiogram results showing severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction, along with the ECG findings of narrow complex tachycardia and elevated brain-type natriuretic peptide, are consistent with tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy. The abrupt changes in heart rate and premature atrial complexes also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While dilated cardiomyopathy could explain the left ventricular systolic dysfunction, it does not directly account for the tachycardia and its potential role in causing the cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Restrictive cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Restrictive cardiomyopathy typically presents with diastolic dysfunction and does not typically cause tachycardia.

rejected.label: Cardiac amyloidosis
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence in the vignette to suggest cardiac amyloidosis, such as characteristic echocardiogram findings or biopsy results.

rejected.label: Atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia
rejected.why: While the patient has tachycardia, the echocardiogram findings and elevated brain-type natriuretic peptide suggest a more complex cardiac issue than just a reentrant tachycardia.
